extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers (PIOs) who are new to the field or less experienced, or established PIOs seeking refresher training
extracted.subtask_description: Two-day FEMA G-290 Basic Public Information Officer (PIO) course teaching foundational public information skills for public safety, emergency management, and government/municipal PIO activities, including media relations and crisis communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended audience / course target
rubrics_metrics.description: This course is intended for Public Information Officers who are new to the field or less experienced, or established PIOs who desire to refresh their training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this course if you are a new or less-experienced PIO or an established PIO seeking to refresh basic PIO skills and knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: The course emphasis is on the basic skills and knowledge needed for public safety, emergency management and government/municipal public information activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training focuses on foundational competencies rather than advanced/specialized PIO topics; appropriate as an entry-level or refresher course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic: role of the PIO
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics include: the role of the PIO
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers responsibilities and functions of a Public Information Officer in public safety and emergency contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic: communications tools
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction will address the tools used for public information work (likely including traditional and digital channels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic: awareness campaigns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers planning and executing public awareness campaigns relevant to public safety and emergency management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic: news release writing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaches how to draft news releases as part of PIO responsibilities (content, format, and distribution considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic: public speaking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes training on speaking to the public and stakeholder groups, likely focusing on clarity, messaging, and presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic: conducting television interviews and news conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics include: conducting television interviews and news conferences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical instruction on interacting with broadcast media and managing press conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic: strategic and crisis communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics include: strategic and crisis communications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses planning and executing communications during crises, including strategy, messaging, and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic: social media
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers use of social media platforms for public information, likely including best practices and rapid information dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite: FEMA Student Identification (SID)
rubrics_metrics.description: You need to have a FEMA Student Identification number, which can be obtained at https://cdp.dhs.gov/femasid/
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain a FEMA SID before registering/attending; it is a required administrative identifier for course records and certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite: completion of FEMA Public Information Awareness IS-29.a
rubrics_metrics.description: You need to have ... completed the FEMA Public Information Awareness IS-29.a. You can complete this course online at http://bit.ly/2oQ1WS9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion of IS-29.a is required before a G-290 certificate will be issued; participants must provide proof of their IS-29.a certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of prerequisite required for certificate issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: You will need to provide proof of your IS-29.a certificate before your G-290 certificate will be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should retain and submit IS-29.a completion documentation to receive the G-290 certificate; without proof, certification is withheld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended (but not required) NIMS courses
rubrics_metrics.description: Strongly recommended, though not required, are the following National Incident Management System (NIMS) courses: IS-100.B (Introduction to the Incident Command System (ICS), IS-200.B (ICS for Single Resources and Initial Action Incidents), IS-700.A (NIMS – An Introduction), IS-800.B (National Response Framework – An Introduction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These NIMS courses enhance preparedness/background for G-290 attendees but are optional; consider completing them to strengthen foundational incident management knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course status in professional development program
rubrics_metrics.description: This is an elective course in the advanced professional series (APS) program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: G-290 counts as an elective toward APS professional development credentials rather than as a mandatory core course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule, duration, and location
rubrics_metrics.description: 9 a.m. – 5 p.m. July 19 & 20, 2021; Sheraton Panama City Beach Golf & Spa Resort, 4114 Jan Cooley Drive, Panama City Beach, FL 32408.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two full-day in-person attendance on specified dates and location; plan travel and lodging accordingly (hotel accommodations information available).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee / registration cost
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tuition/registration cost is $150 per person; register and pay to secure a seat. Event uses Swoogo event management software for registration.
